findings.title: Switching span buffers from sets to sorted sets breaks in-flight Redis data
findings.body: The script and SpansBuffer now use ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZADD/ZSCAN on span-buf:s:* keys, but segments already buffered before deployment are Redis SETs created with SADD. Redis returns WRONGTYPE for sorted-set commands on those keys, so process_spans/flush_segments will error for in-flight segments until their TTL expires (redis_ttl defaults to 3600s), losing or stalling those spans. No migration, type check, or dual-read handling is included.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM and corrupts duplicate span scores
findings.body: Both zunionstore calls omit an AGGREGATE clause, so Redis defaults to SUM. If the same span payload exists in both the destination and source sorted sets (e.g. a re-delivered span, or a span already zadded under the destination key by process_spans before the Lua merge), its score becomes the sum of the two end_timestamp_precise values (roughly double, e.g. year 2077). Eviction via ZPOPMIN then orders by corrupted scores, so duplicated spans are effectively never evicted and eviction order no longer reflects end time. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN) explicitly.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator is incompatible with the datetime ordering of its only caller
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint calls this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key does int(math.floor(value)) on the datetime attribute and value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor value instead of converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does. build_cursor calls get_item_key on every non-empty page (TypeError on datetime) and build_queryset compares the datetime column against an int. The optimized_pagination=true path will therefore 500 or mis-filter for audit logs instead of paginating them.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing raises instead of being handled by Django
findings.body: The advanced-features branch passes cursor.offset (parsed from the user-supplied cursor string) directly as queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start, claiming the Django ORM handles this. Django querysets explicitly raise AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') on negative slices, and the same applies to the is_prev branch in BasePaginator.get_result (line 182-184) which also leaves offset unclamped. Any admin hitting the audit-log endpoint with a crafted negative-offset cursor gets a 500, so the advertised feature does not work and adds a trivial error/DoS path.

findings.title: Unrelated audit-log pagination feature is bundled into the spans change
findings.body: This PR is titled and described as a spans-buffer optimization, but it also adds a new user-controlled 'optimized_pagination' mode to the organization audit-log endpoint, gated on is_superuser/has_global_access and backed by the new OptimizedCursorPaginator. This changes behavior of a sensitive audit-log API (whose paginator is broken for datetime keys and crashes on negative offsets, per the paginator findings) without any endpoint tests, changelog, or feature-flag rollout. It should be split out and reviewed/tested independently rather than shipped hidden inside the spans change.

findings.title: Redirect depth limit silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The redirect-following loop cap drops from 10000 to 1000 and the comment explaining that deeper segment trees may not be joined correctly is deleted. Traces whose parent chain exceeds 1000 redirects will now stop following redirects early, so spans land in separate span-buf:s:* sets and are flushed as fragmented/incomplete segments rather than one segment. This is a correctness regression for deep traces unrelated to the 1000-span eviction cap (chain depth and span count are different dimensions).

findings.title: Flush-side max_segment_spans safeguard removed while insert cap is inconsistent
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer drops segments exceeding max_segment_spans (the metric and logger.error branch were removed), so the only remaining span-count protection is the Lua cap. That cap is hardcoded to 1000 while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans defaults to 1001 and is configurable, and it only runs on the insert path: segments created before this change, created while script loading fails, or grown by the Python-side ZADD pipeline before Lua runs can now be loaded and flushed unbounded (bounded only by the 10MiB byte cap), reintroducing the memory/segment-size risk the removed guard protected against, with no metric when eviction truncates a segment.

findings.title: process_batch now hard-requires end_timestamp_precise and will crash the batch if absent
findings.body: Span previously did not need end_timestamp_precise; the existing consumer test payload omitted it and had to be modified in this PR to add it. Using val['end_timestamp_precise'] raises KeyError for any ingest-spans message lacking the field, failing the entire batch in process_batch (and, under Arroyo, causing redelivery/retry of the same poison batch) instead of defaulting the score (e.g. val.get('end_timestamp_precise', 0) or the message timestamp). Either tolerate a missing value or prove from the schema that it is mandatory and add a test for the missing-field case.

findings.title: No test covers eviction, the sorted-set merge, or the reduced redirect depth
findings.body: The test changes in this PR only add the new end_timestamp_precise argument to existing Span constructions. There is no test that inserts more than 1000 spans into one segment to verify ZPOPMIN eviction (which spans survive, whether the root/segment span can be evicted, and final flushed contents), no test with duplicate payloads across merged sets to verify score handling, and no test near the new 1000 redirect-depth limit. The core behavioral change of the PR is therefore unverified.
